headline: Two sessions of global green and a violent commodity snapback, but the US curve kept flattening into a hiking Fed — the bounce is in beta, not in the plumbing.
summary: The rally that started in Europe on Wednesday went worldwide on Thursday and Friday. Bovespa added another 6.1% (+6.3% on the week) as USDBRL fell 1.4% to 5.82, Euro Stoxx +2.0%, DAX +2.1%, FTSE +1.7%, CAC +1.6%, and Asia finally joined: KOSPI +1.7% after a -20.3% month, Nikkei +0.8%, Hang Seng +0.6%. Commodities caught the most violent bid of all — silver +6.1%, platinum +5.0%, copper +3.5%, gold +2.1%, WTI +2.1% to 85.46 (Brent dissented, -2.6% to 92.11). VIX fell another 5.3% to 26.80, two sessions off the 34 print. Risk regime is -19 from -20. That is the whole good-news list, and it is all price.

The plumbing did not improve. High-yield OAS widened another 9bp to 3.72, IG to 0.98 and BBB to 1.22 — both still pinned at the 100th percentile of the year — and CCC at 14.05 is +520bp YTD; HYG/IEF carries a 1m z of -1.31 and is rolling over. The front end still prices tightening: the 3-month bill at 4.36% against 3.88% effective funds, 99th percentile, acceleration z=0.41, while the 10-year real yield sits at 2.79% with acceleration z=0.69 and 22% above its 200-day. 3m10y flattened a further 4bp to 0.51 (-27bp on the month, z=-0.96) and 2s10s is 0.24 at the 7th percentile. Breakevens are the tell: 5y 2.13% (z=-1.62), 10y 2.12% at the 0th percentile, against core CPI accelerating (z=0.93, turning up). Hot realized inflation, dead forward inflation, inverted vol curve — VIXTS 1.0761, +4.0% today, with VIX3M up 3.2% even as spot VIX fell. The front of the vol curve is draining; the back is still bidding.

The equity bid stays defensive-cyclical and non-AI. RSP/SPY is at a 1m z of 2.88 and the 100th percentile of the year; SPW is turning up, IWM/SPY +0.9%. Against that, SMH is -22.0% on the month and 19.5% below its 200-day, SOXX -21.9%, NVDA -30.9%, MU -33.5%, ORCL -46.0% YTD at the 2nd percentile, MTUM 1m z=-2.93, SPHB/SPLV at the 4th percentile, IWF/IWD at the 5th. What changed inside tech is the funding mix: IGV/SMH is +9.4% on the month and +22.1% in three, with IGV turning up while semis still bleed. Dispersion across countries is now the biggest alpha in the digest: Sensex 1m z=3.45 with acceleration 2.58 and INDA +14.2% on the month (rel +21.9%) versus EWT -21.0% and EWY -15.4%, while USDINR is -3.1% on the month at z=-2.96. Mexico is the new FX stress point Brazil used to be: USDMXN 19.68, 1m z=1.91, 100th percentile, MXX -1.4%.

Two things to re-check from yesterday's read. First, the housing trade's fuel is wobbling — the 30-year mortgage ticked +10bp on the week to 7.21% even though it is -11bp on the month, and building permits are -7.2%; the price action (ITB +9.4% 1m, XHB/SPY z=2.34 with acceleration 1.47, DHI, HD) is still the cleanest domestic uptrend, but it needs the long end to behave with 30s at 5.30%. Second, the consumer tax is getting worse, not better: natural gas +9.9% today to 3.593, +33.2% on the month, acceleration z=1.80, 21% above its 200-day, landing on UMich sentiment of 48. Stay long the median stock, shelter and precious-metals beta; stay short the things 2.79% real yields and a 100th-percentile BBB spread price worst.

good.text: Global breadth, two sessions running: Bovespa +6.1%, DAX +2.1%, Euro Stoxx +2.0%, FTSE +1.7%, KOSPI +1.7% off a -20.3% month, Nikkei +0.8%. EFA/SPY 1m z=1.10 with acceleration z=1.20.
The median US stock is at a record relative high: RSP/SPY +6.0% on the month, 1m z=2.88, 100th percentile of the year, acceleration z=0.72; IWM/SPY +0.9%, SPW turning up.
Credit's second derivative is still improving even as levels worsen: acceleration z of -2.19 on CCC, -0.78 BBB, -0.71 IG, -0.69 HY; LQD +0.5%, BKLN acceleration z=0.59.
Spot vol keeps draining: VIX -5.3% to 26.80, -5.8% on the week, two sessions after a 34 handle; SKEW at the 37th percentile.
Real-economy data is not cracking: initial claims 189,000 (-14.9% y/y, 0th percentile), continuing claims 1.697m, unemployment 4.1%, JOLTS openings +4.6%.
India is the single strongest trend in the book: Sensex 1m z=3.45 with acceleration 2.58, INDA +14.2% on the month and +21.9% relative, financed by USDINR -3.1% at z=-2.96.

bad.text: The curve keeps flattening toward a hike: 3m bill 4.36% vs 3.88% funds (99th pctile), 3m10y 0.51 after -4bp today and -27bp on the month (z=-0.96), 2s10s 0.24 at the 7th percentile.

Real yields are accelerating upward — 10y TIPS 2.79%, acceleration z=0.69, 22% above its 200-day — while 5y and 10y breakevens sit at 2.13% and 2.12%, the 3rd and 0th percentiles, against core CPI turning up (z=0.93).
Credit is still widening into the equity bounce: HY OAS +9bp to 3.72 (+34bp 1m, +102bp 3m), IG 0.98, BBB 1.22, both 100th percentile; HYG/IEF 1m z=-1.31 and rolling over.
Back-end vol is still being bought while spot falls: VIX3M +3.2% to 26.29 (1m +31.8%), VIXTS 1.0761 and +4.0% today — the inversion is widening again, not flipping.
The AI/semis liquidation is slower but unrepaired: SMH -22.0% 1m and 19.5% below its 200-day, SOXX -21.9%, NVDA -30.9%, MU -33.5%, SMH/SPY 1m z=-2.67, MTUM z=-2.93, SPHB/SPLV at the 4th percentile.
Dollar and EM FX stress rotated, not resolved: DXY 103.76 at the 93rd percentile, USDMXN at the 100th (1m z=1.91) with MXX -1.4%, CEW -2.2% on the month, AUDJPY -4.6% 1m at z=-1.78.

trades.name: Short junk credit vs the belly
trades.line: Short HYG vs long IEF: HY +9bp today, IG/BBB 100th pctile
trades.expr: Short HYG against an equal dollar long in IEF; or buy HYG Jan puts financed by selling upside calls.
trades.thesis: Equities bounced for two sessions and credit did not. HY OAS widened again, IG and BBB are both at the 100th percentile of the year, and CCC at 14.05 is +520bp YTD. Spread decompression with a front end priced for a hike is the one trade that works whether the equity bounce extends or fails; carry cost is covered by the Treasury leg.
trades.trigger: HYOAS +9bp on the day to 3.72, +34bp 1m, +102bp 3m, 1m z=1.14. HYG/IEF 1m z=-1.31 and rolling over while SPX only fell 0.3%. IEF turning up with a 1m z of 0.74.
trades.stop: HY OAS back under 3.40 and HYG/IEF reclaiming its 200-day; or a combined 2.5% loss on the pair.
trades.target: HY OAS toward 4.25 and HYG/IEF toward the 3-month lows; +4% on the pair.

trades.name: India over the Asian tech complex
trades.line: Long INDA vs EEM: Sensex 1m z=3.45, USDINR z=-2.96
trades.expr: Long INDA, short equal dollars of EEM (use EWT/EWY as the funding leg if you want the pure semis short).
trades.thesis: India is the only major market making a new relative high with a falling local-currency cost of capital, while the EM index is dominated by Taiwan and Korea semis that are in a 20%+ monthly drawdown. Cheap oil (Brent -19.1% 1m) is a direct Indian terms-of-trade subsidy.
trades.trigger: Sensex +14.6% 1m, 1m z=3.45 with acceleration 2.58; INDA +14.2% 1m, +21.9% relative, turning up. EEM -8.8% 1m with EWT -21.0% and EWY -15.4%. USDINR -3.1% on the month at z=-2.96 versus CEW -2.2%.
trades.stop: USDINR turning back up through its 200-day, or the pair giving back 4%; INDA 9.6% above its 200-day is the extension risk.
trades.target: +6% on the pair as EM index weight in Taiwan/Korea keeps de-rating.

trades.name: Natural gas vs the oil complex
trades.line: Long nat gas vs short XLE: +33% 1m, acc z=1.8, crude rolling
trades.expr: Long front NG futures (or UNG equivalent) against a half-size short in XLE.
trades.thesis: Natural gas is the only commodity in the digest with an intact, accelerating uptrend while the rest of the complex is being liquidated. Energy equities are priced off crude, which keeps rolling over; the heating-season squeeze pays through the molecule, not the oil major.
trades.trigger: NATGAS +9.9% to 3.593, +33.2% 1m, acceleration z=1.80, 21% above its 200-day. Against that DBC 1m z=-2.75 with acceleration -2.24, Brent -2.6% today and -19.1% on the month, gasoline -21.9%, XLE -12.6% 1m with acceleration z=-2.19 and XOM acceleration z=-2.52.
trades.stop: NG closes back below 3.10 (loss of the 200-day extension) or the combined position loses 12%.
trades.target: NG toward 4.20 into mid-winter; +15% on the combined book.

trades.name: Low vol over high beta
trades.line: Long SPLV / short SPHB: vol curve still inverted at 1.076
trades.expr: Long SPLV, short equal dollars of SPHB.
trades.thesis: Spot VIX is falling but the term structure is still inverted and three-month vol is rising — the market is paying up for protection further out while selling the panic. In that regime the de-rating of beta continues, and this pair is the cleanest way to be short the unwind without picking a semi.
trades.trigger: VIXTS 1.0761, +4.0% today, with VIX3M +3.2% even as VIX fell 5.3%. SPHB/SPLV -15.3% on the month, 1m z=-2.35, 4th percentile of the year; SPLV +3.4% 1m and at the 95th percentile while SPHB is 12% below its 200-day.
trades.stop: VIXTS back under 0.95 (term structure normalizes) with SPHB/SPLV reclaiming its 50-day; or -4% on the pair.
trades.target: +6% on the pair toward the 2025 lows in the high-beta ratio.

trades.name: Software over silicon
trades.line: Long IGV / short SMH: ratio +9.4% 1m, semis still -22%
trades.expr: Long IGV, short equal dollars of SMH.
trades.thesis: The AI capex trade is being repriced, and the cost line is the hardware. Software is already turning up on an absolute basis while semis remain 19.5% below the 200-day; a capex pause is a margin tailwind for the software consumer and a revenue hit for the supplier.
trades.trigger: IGV/SMH +9.4% on the month and +22.1% in three, 1m z=1.38 and turning up. IGV turning up with relative strength improving to -1.1% over three months while SMH is -16.7% relative on the month, NVDA -30.9%, MU -33.5%, TSM -19.3%, ASML -18.0%.
trades.stop: SMH reclaims its 200-day or NVDA puts in two consecutive 5% up days on volume; -6% on the pair.
trades.target: +8% on the pair, ratio back toward its 3-month high.

trades.name: Housing beta against the index
trades.line: Long ITB vs SPY: ITB +9.4% 1m, XHB/SPY z=2.34
trades.expr: Long ITB against an equal dollar short in SPY (or buy ITB Feb calls outright for convexity).
trades.thesis: Housing is the only intact domestic uptrend in the digest and it is leveraged to the one thing the market now expects a hiking Fed to deliver: demand destruction and a lower long end. Starts rebounded 9.9% and the builders are being re-rated off depressed sentiment.
trades.trigger: ITB +2.9% on Wednesday, +9.4% 1m, turning up with acceleration z=0.79; XHB/SPY +13.0% on the month, 1m z=2.34 with acceleration 1.47; DHI +3.1%, HD +13.1% 1m. Mortgage 7.21%, -11bp on the month.
trades.stop: The 30-year mortgage keeps backing up — it already ticked +10bp on the week — and 30y Treasuries break above 5.45%; or -5% on the pair.
trades.target: +7% relative to SPY as the ratio retakes the 60th percentile.

trades.name: Peso stress, real relief
trades.line: Long USDMXN vs short USDBRL: stress baton moves to Mexico
trades.expr: Long USDMXN forward, short USDBRL forward, equal notional; roll monthly.
trades.thesis: The EM FX blow-up is rotating. Brazil's squeeze is unwinding violently — Bovespa +6.1% and USDBRL -1.4% — while Mexico is only starting to price tariff risk, with the peso already at the extreme of its range and local equities diverging from the global rally.
trades.trigger: USDMXN 19.677, +5.3% 1m, 1m z=1.91, 100th percentile, with MXX -1.4% on a day everyone else rallied. USDBRL -1.4% to 5.82 with acceleration z=0.91 rolling and EWZ +2.9%. CEW -2.2% on the month confirms the basket is still heavy.
trades.stop: USDMXN closes back below 19.00 or USDBRL breaks 6.05 (Brazil stress returns); -3% on the pair.
trades.target: +4% on the pair; USDMXN 20.4 against USDBRL 5.60.
